417	## 5. Draft the PRD
418	
419	Synthesize into a structured PRD using `<SKILL_DIR>/templates/prd-template.md` as the
420	format. Sections:
421	
422	**Authoring style.** Prefer structured markdown — tables and nested lists — over prose
423	paragraphs unless prose is genuinely warranted; flow-shaped content (system/user flows,
424	before → after comparisons) is never rendered as an arrow-paragraph. Mermaid diagrams are
425	at the planner's discretion (the pre-run research findings carry no evidence on mermaid's
426	effect on model comprehension either way) — never required. Every section follows
427	this, except the Problem Statement's plain-language lead, which is prose.
428	
429	- **Goal line** — a single `**Goal:** <one sentence>` line directly under the PRD's
430	  feature-title `#` heading, before `## Problem Statement`. One sentence, ≤30 words,
431	  outcome-phrased — names the observable result, not the mechanism. A vacuous
432	  restatement of the title or the request ("implement the feature described below")
433	  violates the contract: brevity is a contract requirement, not a style preference.
434	  Always present — no omit-when-empty carve-out. See the "Goal line" sub-section below.
435	- **Problem Statement** — opens with a plain-language lead of 2–4 sentences (no anchors,
436	  tables, lists, or internal identifiers) written for a reader with no context, in
437	  reading order: what the affected thing is for, what goes wrong or is missing today, and
438	  what that costs the reader; when the premise does not hold, the lead says so plainly.
439	  Evidence, tables, and anchors follow the lead. Then what problem this solves and why it
440	  matters (not solution language). When step 3's premise check fails, follow the lead
441	  with a `**Premise check:**` line naming what was assumed vs. what the codebase shows,
442	  and set `## Recommendation` to a non-`Proceed` verdict; omit-when-sound (no line when the stated premise holds). A
443	  threaded `PROMPT-SANITY: <note>` (triage's Prompt sanity gate reached `suspect`) counts
444	  as evidence for this check, and any attached/referenced file is cross-checked against
445	  the request's claims regardless of whether a note was threaded.
446	- **Request vetting** — always-present — a falsifiable hypothesis, a sourced case against
447	  the request's chosen approach, and a closed verdict. See the "Request vetting"
448	  sub-section below for the full contract.
449	- **Existing-code assessment** — always-present — a keep / simplify / rewrite verdict for
450	  every existing surface the plan touches. See the "Existing-code assessment" sub-section
451	  below for the full contract.
452	- **Epic context** (omit-when-empty) — only when step 1.7 detects epic membership: the
453	  epic slug, this feature's id and rationale, its `dependsOn` edges with produced/consumed
454	  artifacts, its downstream dependents, and a `**Manifest write-back:**` line. See the
455	  "Epic context" sub-section in `<SKILL_DIR>/references/discovery-survey-epic.md`. When any
456	  layer of step 1.7 detects epic membership, **MUST Read `<SKILL_DIR>/references/discovery-survey-epic.md` before authoring `## Epic context`.**
457	- **Method selection** (omit-when-no-`SURVEY:`-marker) — only when step 1.8's blind
458	  method survey ran; omit the heading entirely when the marker was absent from the
459	  invocation. When the spawn prompt carries `SURVEY:`, **MUST Read `<SKILL_DIR>/references/discovery-survey-epic.md` before weighing the survey.**
460	- **Scope Boundary** — what's in and what's explicitly out.
461	- **Behavioral contrast** — `### User flow` and `### System flow` before → after
462	  subsections (explicit `none` affirmation allowed), closing with a one-line `**Lost:**`
463	  affirmation. See the "Behavioral contrast" sub-section below for the full contract.
464	- **User Stories / Acceptance Criteria** — testable criteria as "Given/When/Then". Each acceptance criterion must name an externally-failable check — something that can fail without a human looking at it: `a test that runs`, `a file in the expected shape`, or `a command exit code`. "It looks right" is not a check — a criterion a machine cannot falsify provides no regression signal and degrades into manual prose at the `## Test Steps` gate (step 7). This is a strong default, not an absolute MUST: it defers to the genuinely-manual carve-out one stage downstream (subjective UX, cross-browser rendering, performance-under-load criteria are legitimately human-judgment and cannot name an exit code — see the manual-prose carve-out in step 7's automation test), so do not force an author to fake an exit-code check for an irreducibly subjective item.
465	- **Visual Spec** (omit-when-empty) — only when the step 1.6 design-artifact gate fired: per-surface element-level assertion bullets, each tagged with its `spec.json` assertion id and `mechanical`/`judged` tier, placed immediately after User Stories / Acceptance Criteria. See the "Visual Spec" sub-section in `<SKILL_DIR>/references/discovery-ui.md` for the full contract; omit the heading entirely otherwise.
466	- **Layout Intent** (omit-when-empty) — only when the plan touches UI: per-surface structural layout the user ratifies at plan-pending-review (see the `### Layout Intent` sub-section in `<SKILL_DIR>/references/discovery-ui.md`). Omit the heading entirely for non-UI plans.
467	- **Instrumentation** — always-present: the metrics, dashboard-panel and alert/SLO spec for every runtime surface the plan adds or changes (a request handler, background job or queue consumer, outbound API call, multi-stage pipeline, or connection or worker pool), or a single `none — <reason>` line. **MUST Read `<SKILL_DIR>/references/discovery-instrumentation.md` before authoring a non-`none` `## Instrumentation` section.**
468	- **Architecture Decisions** — from the checkpoint above. Its `### Runtime design` subsection is always present: **MUST Read `<SKILL_DIR>/references/discovery-runtime-design.md` before authoring it.**
469	- **Technical Constraints** — every bullet binding and source-traceable (a named file,
470	  rule, or research finding); ambient repo-convention restatements are banned unless the
471	  plan turns on them; an explicit `none beyond repo-wide conventions` affirmation is
472	  allowed; a named performance/cost-implications category (latency, token spend, CI time)
473	  is emitted only when the change plausibly moves one.
474	- **Open Questions** — every assumption you made plus anything still unresolved. Each
475	  entry must name what changes on redirect — a question whose every answer leaves the
476	  plan unchanged is deleted, not written (earns-its-place rule). Every entry also carries
477	  a resolution marker — see the "Open Questions (resolution-first)" sub-section below.
478	- **Decision analysis** (omit-when-empty) — for each _consequential_ open decision whose
479	  branches genuinely diverge, illustrate each branch's downstream end-user/system flow, mark
480	  exclusive vs complementary, enumerate + rank the viable combinations, and give a verdict that
481	  feeds the Recommendation; omit the heading entirely when no such decision exists. See the
482	  "Decision analysis" sub-section below for the full contract.
483	- **Alternatives considered** (omit-when-empty) — ≤3 one-line entries recording paths
484	  discovery closed, each rejection reason concrete and verifiable; omit the heading
485	  entirely when no path was closed. See the "Alternatives considered" sub-section below.
486	- **Recommendation** — a single clear recommendation; see the "Recommendation"
487	  sub-section below for the verdict enum and one-line-rationale contract.
488	- **Plan risks** — an always-present single line naming the plan's single weakest
489	  assumption / biggest risk; see the "Plan risks" sub-section below for the
490	  always-present/single-line contract.
491	- **Cut list** — an always-present 1-3 bullets naming unnecessary complexity in the
492	  plan that slows shipping, or an explicit `nothing — plan is minimal` affirmation; see
493	  the "Cut list" sub-section below for the full contract.
494	- **Prompt interpretation** (conditional) — when the prompt names BOTH prescribed
495	  methods AND a quantitative target; see the "Prompt interpretation (conditional)"
496	  sub-section in `<SKILL_DIR>/references/discovery-prompt-interpretation.md` for the full contract.
497	  **MUST Read `<SKILL_DIR>/references/discovery-prompt-interpretation.md` when the request prescribes methods AND names a quantitative target, before authoring `## Prompt interpretation`.**
498	
499	Load `<SKILL_DIR>/references/example-prd.md` (if present) to match the project's
500	PRD style.
501	
502	### Candidate follow-up issues (optional)
503	
504	If discovery surfaces orthogonal ideas the user did **not** ask for but that the codebase or
505	the user's verbatim description suggests are worth tracking, capture them as a separate
506	section that the supervisor will route through `flow-create-issue` post-merge. This is
507	distinct from "Open Questions": Open Questions are assumptions about _this_ feature that
508	the user should confirm; candidate follow-up issues are _next-time_ work the user can
509	opt into.
510	
511	**Objective-item triage (bundle by default).** Default to bundling adjacent work into
512	`# Task breakdown` at authoring time rather than parking it as a candidate follow-up:
513	bundle clear UX additions and enhancements, bug fixes plus their tests, code quality
514	improvements, testing improvements, and small or prerequisite refactors — include
515	anything that should reasonably and ultimately be a part of the feature anyway.
516	Borderline ties break toward bundle. An item remains eligible for the candidate
517	follow-up section ONLY under one of four named exclusions:
518	
519	1. a **genuinely novel non-trivial feature** — its own user goal and surface, not a
520	   natural extension of this one;
521	2. it needs its own design/decision session — the rationale MUST name the specific
522	   open decision that needs its own session; a rationale naming no nameable decision
523	   is a bundling miss, not a valid exclusion;
524	3. a large refactor that is not a prerequisite for this feature — heuristics: it
525	   would roughly double the diff, or touches many files the feature otherwise
526	   would not.
527	4. **user-foreclosed** — the user's request or SCOPE AND CONSTRAINTS block rules it
528	   out; the Rationale MUST quote the user's constraint verbatim in double quotes
529	   (precedent: issue #762).
530	
531	**Hardening rule.** Exclusion 3's size test applies to the bundle SET
532	**cumulatively**, not per-candidate: several individually-fine bundles can together
533	roughly double the diff. Apply the test to the bundle set as a whole; on overflow,
534	keep the highest-value bundles in the task breakdown and demote the rest to
535	candidates, ticked only when their block clears the bar.
536	
537	**Small/Low rule.** A candidate whose Complexity is Trivial or Small AND whose Risk
538	is Low is objective by presumption — bundle it. It survives as a candidate ONLY under
539	`genuinely novel non-trivial feature`, `user-foreclosed`, or a design/decision
540	exclusion whose Rationale names the decision — any of "open decision" (e.g.
541	`the open decision is …`), "decision is", "specifically", or "the (specific)
542	decision" clears it; a rationale that merely asserts a design session exists
543	with no nameable decision does not. `large refactor` never applies to a
544	Small item. `flow-candidate-issues --lint`
545	reports the misses as `exclusion-missing`, `decision-unnamed`, and
546	`small-low-risk`.
547	
548	For example: "the retry loop swallows the underlying error" is an objective bug —
549	bundle it into the task breakdown. "Add a settings toggle to let users disable
550	retries" is a UX addition adjacent to this feature — bundle it too, unless it needs
551	its own design session (name the decision) or the bundle set would double in size.
552	"Migrate the entire auth stack to a new provider" is a genuinely novel non-trivial
553	feature — that stays a candidate. Likewise, "off-by-one in the pagination cursor"
554	bundles into the current task. Author `# Task breakdown` BEFORE `# Candidate
555	follow-up issues` (authoring order only — the on-disk section order in step 8 is
556	unchanged), so adjacent work is consumed by the task list before a candidate
557	section exists to park it in. After authoring both sections, run a
558	**mutual-exclusion self-check**: verify no item appears in BOTH `# Task breakdown`
559	and `# Candidate follow-up issues` — dedup by intent (the same underlying change
560	described two ways), not by string match — and fold any duplicate found back into
561	the task breakdown, removing it from the candidate table.
562	
563	When (and only when) such ideas exist, add a top-level `# Candidate follow-up issues`
564	section to `plan.md`, placed between `# PRD` and `# Task breakdown` (see step 8). The
565	section has **two parts, in this order**: a value-vs-complexity **ranking table**, then
566	the machine-readable `- [ ]` checkbox list. Each checkbox is a single-line title-and-body entry followed by its indented value-prop block (the six labelled sub-bullets defined below):
567	
568	```markdown
569	# Candidate follow-up issues
570	
571	| Candidate                       | Value | Complexity | Rationale                             | Relation to current request | Pull into this pipeline? |
572	| ------------------------------- | ----- | ---------- | ------------------------------------- | --------------------------- | ------------------------ |
573	| OAuth refresh path leaks tokens | High  | Medium     | real security gap but its own session | unrelated to this feature   | No                       |
574	| Pin `gh-action-cache` to v4     | Low   | Trivial    | one-line CI bump, unblocks nothing    | unrelated to this feature   | No                       |
575	
576	- [x] OAuth refresh path leaks tokens — separate concern; needs a dedicated session.
577	  - **UX:** none
578	  - **Problem:** refresh tokens are logged in plaintext on every retry [anchor: src/auth/oauth-client.ts:88]
579	  - **Stability/efficiency:** none
580	  - **Value rank:** 5 — a live credential leak with no workaround [anchor: src/auth/oauth-client.ts:88]
581	  - **Complexity:** Small — one file, isolated to the OAuth client
582	  - **Risk:** High — needs its own security-review session
583	  - **If never done:** the leak persists in every future auth-touching PR
584	  - **Verdict:** clears bar — a live credential leak outweighs Complexity and Risk
585	- [ ] `gh-action-cache@v3` is deprecated — pin to v4 in CI.
586	  - **UX:** none
587	  - **Problem:** none
588	  - **Stability/efficiency:** none
589	  - **Value rank:** 1 — cosmetic version bump, no observed failure or deprecation deadline [anchor: `gh-action-cache@v3` still passing in CI]
590	  - **Complexity:** Trivial — one line in CI config
591	  - **Risk:** Low
592	  - **If never done:** nothing — v3 keeps working until GitHub removes it
593	  - **Verdict:** below bar — no observed failure or deprecation deadline, just a version bump
594	```
595	
596	**The ranking table is mandatory whenever the section is present** (it is not itself
597	omit-when-present — only the whole section is omit-when-empty). It forces an explicit
598	value/complexity judgment per candidate so a cheap-and-valuable item is never silently
599	parked as a follow-up when it should have been pulled into the current pipeline. Rows
600	should be ordered by Value (High → Low). Columns are exactly
601	`Candidate | Value | Complexity | Rationale | Relation to current request | Pull into this pipeline?`.
602	Each Rationale cell must state why the item matters (the underlying reason it is worth
603	tracking), never merely restating the candidate's title. The `Relation to current
604	request` column names how the candidate connects to (or diverges from) the work this
605	plan is about — the supervisor's `--details` disclosure block and the `pull #N into the
606	plan` redirect offer read this column to help the user decide. The `Pull into this pipeline?`
607	column carries **plain `Yes` / `No` text — never a `- [ ]`
608	checkbox**: the checkbox list BELOW the table is the sole machine-readable candidate
609	contract (`flow-candidate-issues` parses only `- [ ]` / `- [x]` lines, so a checkbox in a
610	table cell would be a parser-mis-read hazard). Value and Complexity are coarse buckets
611	(`High`/`Medium`/`Low` and `Trivial`/`Small`/`Medium`/`Large`).
612	
613	**Exclusion-naming rule.** Each candidate's Rationale cell in the ranking table MUST
614	name which of the four named exclusions applies —
615	`genuinely novel non-trivial feature`, needs its own design/decision session, a
616	large refactor that is not a prerequisite, or `user-foreclosed: "<quoted
617	constraint>"` — and, for the design/decision exclusion, the specific open decision
618	that needs its own session. A Rationale cell that names no exclusion is a bundling
619	miss: fold the item into `# Task breakdown` instead of leaving it as a candidate.
620	`/flow-pipeline` step 3 runs `flow-candidate-issues --lint`; a `bundlingMisses`
621	entry triggers ONE automatic revision pass that pulls the item into the task
622	breakdown before the plan is shown — write the exclusion honestly or bundle the
623	item yourself.
624	
625	**Consistency rubric (follow-up references must resolve).** Any item the plan prose refers
626	to as "listed as a follow-up" / "tracked as a follow-up" / "deferred to a follow-up" (or a
627	sibling phrasing) MUST actually appear as a checkbox in this section — a prose reference to
628	a follow-up that does not exist in the list is the exact drift an external reviewer caught
629	in the econ-data run. After the plan lands, the supervisor runs
630	`flow-candidate-issues --lint --plan-md-file <plan.md>` as a deterministic advisory
631	backstop; author the section so that check passes (every referenced follow-up is listed).
632	
633	Tick (`- [x]`) only a candidate whose value-prop block reads `**Verdict:** clears bar`;
634	author every other candidate unticked (`- [ ]`). Unticked candidates stay in the
635	ranking table and the checkbox list and are shown by `--details`; they file only if
636	the user replies `file candidate #N`. Unclear ⇒ unticked.
637	No `AskUserQuestion` form fires anywhere in this flow; instead, the supervisor echoes
638	`flow-candidate-issues --details` at plan presentation so the user sees the full
639	candidate list inline. The user curates by replying with one of four verbs:
640	`pull #N into the plan` (moves a candidate into this pipeline's task breakdown),
641	`drop candidate #N` (unticks it, removing it from the file-on-merge set),
642	`defer task #N` (moves a task-breakdown item back out to a ticked candidate), or
643	`file candidate #N` (ticks it).
644	Whatever stays ticked when the PR merges is what the step-10 post-merge sweep files
645	via `flow-create-issue`.
646	
647	If discovery surfaces no orthogonal ideas, **omit the section entirely** — do not write an
648	empty heading. An empty heading is a no-op for the supervisor (count is `0` → empty
649	`--details` output, nothing to disclose), but it implies candidates exist when none do, adds noise to plan review,
650	and risks accumulating stale `- [ ]` entries on later edits. The supervisor's
651	"section absent" and "count is 0" branches behave identically; the value of omitting
652	the heading is signal-to-noise, not control flow.
653	
654	Bar for inclusion: the four named exclusions in **Objective-item triage** above are
655	the entire bar — a genuinely novel non-trivial feature, an item that needs its own
656	design/decision session (naming the specific decision), a large refactor that is
657	not a prerequisite (applied cumulatively across the whole bundle set), or
658	`user-foreclosed` (the user's own constraint, quoted verbatim). Per the
659	AGENTS.md `## Output style` rule
660	**Treat every request as production-bound, not a hobby project.**, the include-vs-defer
661	test is cohesion, not size; do not use this section as a hedge to defer cohesive
662	in-scope work that fails all four exclusions. A backlog full of low-confidence
663	candidates is still noise — when in doubt, bundle.
664	
665	<!-- flow-value-rubric:begin -->
666	
667	**Value-prop block** — required before an item is ticked, filed, deferred, or verdicted DO / NEEDS-DECISION.
668	
669	- **UX:** <who notices, what changes for them, how often / how much> `[anchor: …]` — or `none`
670	- **Problem:** <the concrete failure or friction this removes> `[anchor: …]` — or `none`
671	- **Stability/efficiency:** <crash / flake / cost / latency effect, with the reproduced or measured number> `[anchor: …]` — or `none`
672	- **Value rank:** `1`-`5` `[anchor: …]` — the highest rank whose condition is met: `5` data loss, security exposure, or a broken path with no workaround; `4` a user-visible failure with a workaround recurring on a named cadence; `3` a measured inefficiency with a number; `2` a single-instance annoyance or an unfired latent risk; `1` cosmetic
673	- **Complexity:** `Trivial` | `Small` | `Medium` | `Large` — <files touched, blast radius>
674	- **Risk:** `Low` | `Medium` | `High` — <review load, regression risk>
675	- **If never done:** <what breaks, stays broken, or keeps costing — or `nothing`>
676	- **Verdict:** `clears bar` | `below bar` — <the decisive line, and why it outweighs (or fails to outweigh) Complexity and Risk>
677	
678	**Short form.** For a genuinely trivial item (a typo, a dead link), skip the full block and write one line instead: `**Short form:** [V:n|C:x|R:y] <one-line text> [anchor: …]`. The compact tuple keeps the item sortable — the short form drops the prose, never the rank.
679	
680	**Anchor rule.** Every non-`none` UX / Problem / Stability line, and the Value rank, ends with `[anchor: …]` drawn from this closed list: a `file:line`; a reproduced behaviour (`command → observed output`); a command that fails today; a merged PR or commit; an issue number with its age; a measured number; the user's own words, quoted. A value line with no anchor is `unsubstantiated` and counts as `none`; a rank with no anchor is invalid — it cannot be falsified by opening it. Write file anchors bare (`[anchor: path/to/file.ts:42]`), never wrapped in backticks, so the lint can check the path exists.
681	
682	**Bar.** `clears bar` requires at least one substantiated value line, a `Value rank` of `2` or higher, a one-line rationale that it outweighs Complexity and Risk, and a non-`nothing` If-never-done line. `Value rank: 2` is the normal clear-bar baseline, not a special case — most items that clear the bar clear it at `2`. Anything else — including unclear — is `below bar`.
683	
684	**Banned phrasing.** `nicer`, `cleaner`, `could improve`, `might`, `best practice`, `would be good to`, `likely`. An anchor the reader cannot open or run in seconds is worse than `none` — never invent one.
685	
686	<!-- flow-value-rubric:end -->
687	
688	### Request vetting
689	
690	**Always present.** Every plan.md argues against the request's chosen approach — a
691	confidently-framed request executed exactly as framed, with no stage ever asking whether
692	the approach itself is sound, is the failure mode this section exists to close (issue
693	#805). `flow-plan-lint`'s `checkRequestVetting` enforces the shape below; a miss is
694	advisory (never blocks planning) but is always named.
695	
696	Four required labelled lines, in this order:
697	
698	- `- **Hypothesis:**` — the falsifiable claim the plan rests on (what has to be true for
699	  the chosen approach to work).
700	- `- **Case against:**` — the best evidence AGAINST the chosen approach: same-model
701	  self-critique without external grounding does not reliably help (the exact failure mode
702	  this check exists to prevent), so at least one line here must cite either a committed
703	  repo path or a URL — `[anchor: <committed path or URL>]` or a bare `http(s)://` link.
704	  **Never cite a `.flow-tmp/` path** — that directory is excluded from git and deleted by
705	  `flow-remove-worktree` on merge, so an anchor into it is unresolvable the moment the PR
706	  ships; cite the COMMITTED file the claim is really about instead. The block must also
707	  clear a 15-word floor — a trivially-true one-liner ("this could be simpler [anchor:
708	  x]") is exactly the same-model self-critique the research behind this section found
709	  does not work.
710	- `- **Sources:**` — what grounded the case against: a URL, or the exact literal
711	  `no outside source: <reason>` when none was available. This line makes the common
712	  no-research/no-review case VISIBLE rather than silently passing as if it were grounded.
713	- `- **Verdict:**` — closed grammar, exact-match, one of:
714	  - `adopt` — the request's approach stands as asked.
715	  - `adopt-with-conditions: <measurable condition>` — proceeds, with a named condition.
716	  - `push back: <alternative>` — the case against wins; name the alternative.
717	
718	  A non-`adopt` verdict requires a `## Decision analysis` section elsewhere in the plan —
719	  it is the fork the verdict resolves into. **The task breakdown follows this verdict, not
720	  the request as literally written** — a `push back` or `adopt-with-conditions` verdict
721	  must be reflected in which tasks actually ship (see this file's own dogfooded section
722	  for a worked example).
723	
724	Additional free-form body lines (e.g. `- **Per-part:**` for a multi-part request that
725	needs a per-part verdict) are permitted and count against the ceiling below like any
726	other line — they are not part of the four required labels.
727	
728	**Ceiling.** ≤12 non-blank BODY lines (the `## Request vetting` heading itself is not
729	counted). Keep it short — a long section is the ceremony this contract exists to prevent,
730	not evidence of rigor.
731	
732	**Grounding availability.** The Step 1.5(c) `refute-approach` research entry (when
733	research runs) is a BONUS grounding source for the case against, not a precondition —
734	Step 1.5 does not run on most pipelines (it requires `research.discovery: true` AND the
735	relevance gate AND agy availability). The PRIMARY grounding path is an in-repo `[anchor:
736	<committed path>]` citation; do not stall waiting for a research artifact that will not
737	exist on the common run.
738	
739	**Short form for goal-only requests.** A trivial, single-outcome request may use a
740	one-line case against: hypothesis, `- **Case against:** none material — <why>`, `adopt`
741	— the same anchor/word-count/Sources bar still applies to `<why>`.
742	
743	### Existing-code assessment
744	
745	An always-present `## Existing-code assessment` section, placed directly after `## Request vetting`. One bullet per existing surface the plan touches:
746	
747	`- **<repo path or surface>:** keep | simplify | rewrite — <why> [anchor: path[:line]]`
748	
749	When no existing surface is touched, write the literal line `none — no existing surface touched`. Do not label these bullets `- **Verdict:**` — that prefix belongs to `## Request vetting` alone.
750	
751	- **keep** — the shape fits; extend in place.
752	- **simplify** — extend after a small local cleanup; bundle that cleanup into `# Task breakdown`.
753	- **rewrite** — extending would compound debt. A rewrite that is a prerequisite for the feature becomes a bundled task; otherwise it is a ticked candidate under the large-refactor exclusion.
754	
755	Any non-`keep` verdict is named in `## Recommendation`. Anchors cite committed paths only — never a `.flow-tmp/` path.
756	
757	### Goal line
758	
759	A single `**Goal:** <one sentence>` line, placed directly under the PRD's feature-title
760	`#` heading (before `## Problem Statement`). One sentence, ≤30 words, outcome-phrased —
761	names the observable result, not the mechanism (e.g. "scoped access requested via a
762	magic link" rather than "implement magic-link auth"). A vacuous restatement of the title
763	or the request ("implement the feature described below") violates the contract: brevity
764	is a contract requirement, not a style preference. Always present — no
765	omit-when-empty carve-out, unlike the sections below it.
766	
767	### Behavioral contrast
768	
769	Always present — two subsections showing the observable delta:
770	
771	- `### User flow` — a `Before | After` table (or, when there is no user-facing surface,
772	  explicit `none`) naming what a user experiences differently.
773	- `### System flow` — a short before → after nested list (or explicit `none`) narrating
774	  the delta at the system/consumer level.
775	
776	Closes with a single `**Lost:**` line naming what a user or downstream consumer gives
777	up — explicit `none` is allowed but legitimate ONLY on genuinely additive changes: when
778	the diff removes, replaces, or deprecates anything, the `**Lost:**` line must name it
779	(anti-rubber-stamp guard). Never render this section as an arrow-paragraph — see the
780	structured-markdown authoring-style paragraph above.
781	
782	### Alternatives considered
783	
784	Omit-when-empty: when discovery closed zero plausible paths, omit the
785	`## Alternatives considered` heading entirely — same discipline as `## Decision analysis`
786	below. When ≥1 path was closed, ≤3 one-line entries of the form:
787	
788	```markdown
789	- **<alternative>** — rejected: <why>
790	```
791	
792	Each rejection reason must be concrete and verifiable — a named constraint or a
793	`file:line` pointer, not a vibe ("too complex" is not a reason; "breaks the `# PRD`
794	first-heading anchor `flow-research-note` inserts under, see step 8" is). This section
795	records CLOSED paths (a decision already made); `## Decision analysis` records OPEN
796	forks (a decision still being simulated) — a path belongs in exactly one of the two,
797	never both. Consumed downstream by the scout's `## anti_patterns` (a closed path is
798	never re-proposed) and by `/flow-pr-review`'s `## Foreclosed Paths`.
799	
800	Whenever this section is non-empty, ALSO write a sibling `.flow-tmp/excluded-paths.json`
801	(next to `plan.md`, created with the same `mkdir -p .flow-tmp` step 8 uses) mirroring
802	each bullet: `{"version": 1, "excluded": [{"id": "<kebab-slug>", "path": "<the rejected
803	approach, one line>", "reason": "<the same concrete, verifiable reason>"}]}`, one entry
804	per prose bullet. Omit the JSON file entirely when the section is absent. A revision
805	pass rewrites both together, in lockstep with the plan.
806	
807	### Open Questions (resolution-first)
808	
809	Every unchecked `- [ ]` entry in `## Open Questions` must carry exactly one of two
810	markers, so the reviewer reads a resolved recommendation, not a bare question:
811	
812	- `**Recommended:** <answer> — <one-line rationale naming the decisive rubric
813	factor(s)>` (per the Resolution rubric in discovery-playbook.md), OR
814	- `**Needs user input:** <named reason>` — the reason MUST come from this closed
815	  list: a user-held preference or subjective taste; an external fact the agent
816	  cannot verify; credentials or production access.

983	
984	After weighing the options, the necessity check, and the trade-offs from step 3, commit to
985	**one** recommendation and record it as a short, always-present `## Recommendation` section
986	in the PRD. Unlike `# Candidate follow-up issues` and `## Prompt interpretation` — which are

991	`Verdict:` line. The verdict is one of:
992	
993	- **Proceed** — build the request as scoped.
994	- **Reconsider scope** — build, but with a named scope change (narrower, wider, or a
995	  middle-ground option surfaced under the binary-framing check).
996	- **Defer** — the request is reasonable but better sequenced after other work; name the

998	- **Reject — do nothing** — the request is not necessary; doing nothing (or pointing the
999	  user at an existing capability) serves them better. This is a first-class verdict, not a
1000	  failure to plan — when the necessity check (step 3) lands here, say so plainly.

1002	When the verdict is anything other than `Proceed`, the rationale should reference the
1003	relevant Open Question so the user can redirect at the next `plan-pending-review`
1004	checkpoint. The recommendation is advisory — the user always has the final say at the

1007	**Worth-pursuing verdict stated explicitly.** The verdict IS the "is this worth
1008	pursuing?" answer — state it explicitly as one of the four enum values above rather than
1009	leaving it implied by silence or by the absence of a `Reject` verdict; a `## Recommendation`

1012	`Reject — do nothing`, and reference the Problem Statement's `**Premise check:**` line in

1024	
1025	After committing to a recommendation, name the plan's single weakest assumption / biggest risk and record it as an always-present `## Plan risks` section in the PRD. 1042	## 6. Task Breakdown
1043	
1044	Break the PRD into logical, atomic tasks. Each task tagged with the recommended skill.
1045	
1046	**Task sizing:** A task is the right size if it touches 1–3 files in one domain area
1047	and can be verified with a single check. A task is also bounded to a single logical commit
1048	— as a strong default, ~≤400 changed LOC across 1–3 files — because
1049	Sonnet-class implementer models degrade non-linearly beyond that
1050	(per-generation output caps trigger truncation). Split a task if:
1051	
1052	- It spans multiple languages or runtimes (e.g., backend service + frontend client).
1053	- It creates a new DB table AND uses it in domain logic — migration is one task,
1054	  domain model is another.
1055	- It involves both creating a component and writing its tests.
1056	- Its Contract implies more than ~400 changed LOC — split along the Contract's
1057	  file or interface seams.
1058	
1059	Never split an atomic change to satisfy the LOC number — every task must leave
1060	the repo verify-green on its own, so cohesion wins over the numeric target.
1061	
1062	**Dependency ordering** — follow the layer order:
1063	
1064	1. Database migration (schema, RLS, triggers, RPCs)
1065	2. Generated DB types
1066	3. Backend proxy handler (if external API)
1067	4. Domain model (entity, DTO, repository)
1068	5. Domain store (reactive state)
1069	6. UI components (pages, components, layouts)
1070	7. Integration wiring (connecting layers, route setup)
1071	8. Tests (unit + integration per layer)
1072	
1073	**Format each task as:**
1074	
1075	```markdown
1076	### Task N: [Short Title]
1077	
1078	- **Skill:** `skill-name`
1079	- **Bundled:** <one-line origin>
1080	- **Description:** What to implement
1081	- **Inputs:** What must exist before this task starts
1082	- **Outputs:** What this task produces
1083	- **Contract:**
1084	  - **Files:** repo-relative paths to create/edit (mark create vs edit)
1085	  - **Interfaces:** exact function/type/interface signatures + exported symbols this task decides
1086	  - **Call-site edits:** each consumer edit, named as file + symbol (what changes at every call site)
1087	- **Acceptance criteria:** a runnable command whose exit code verifies the task (e.g. `npm run test -- <file>`, `grep -q '<anchor>' <path>`), not prose
1088	```
1089	
1090	The `- **Contract:**` block is **required on every task** — it is the surgical
1091	half of the breakdown that lets a downstream implementer execute to the
1092	planner's interface decisions instead of re-deriving them. The
1093	`- **Acceptance criteria:**` bullet is a **runnable command** (a deterministic
1094	check that exits 0 when the task is done), not a prose description; reserve
1095	prose only for a genuinely subjective criterion.
1096	
1097	The `- **Bundled:**` bullet is **required on every task that originated as a
1098	bundled candidate** under the Objective-item triage rule above — a one-line
1099	origin naming what adjacent item it absorbed (e.g. `- **Bundled:** the
1100	settings-toggle UX addition surfaced during discovery`). Omit the bullet
1101	entirely on tasks that were always part of the requested feature. This is a
1102	**prose contract**, read by humans and by `/flow-pr-review` to understand scope
1103	provenance — it is NEVER machine-parsed; no helper may grow a parser for it.
1104	
1105	**Per-change-type surgical forms.** The `Interfaces:` / `Call-site edits:`
1106	sub-bullets assume callable boundaries. When a task's change type has none,
1107	substitute the change-type-appropriate surgical form — the same Contract slot,
1108	equally exact:
1109	
1110	| Change type    | Surgical form for the Contract block                                                     |
1111	| -------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
1112	| Code / API     | Exact signatures, exported symbols, and named call-site edits (the default above)        |
1113	| UI / visual    | Exact selectors/components, design tokens, and before → after values per visual property |
1114	| Config / infra | Exact file + key path + before → after values for every key touched                      |
1115	| Docs / prose   | Exact insertion anchor (heading or verbatim phrase) + what is inserted/replaced at it    |
1116	| Schema         | Exact DDL (CREATE/ALTER statements, column types, constraints, policies)                 |

1119	the implementer, not a straitjacket: it is authored before any code exists in
1120	the worktree, so a named file, symbol, or signature may be contradicted by the
1121	actual code at implement time. Downstream consumers verify each claim against
1122	the codebase and, on contradiction, prefer the code, adapt, and record the
1123	deviation explicitly (the scout as a `PLAN-DEVIATION:` bullet in its
1124	`## open_questions`; the coder in `rejected_alternatives`) rather than silently
1125	following or silently rewriting the plan. Specify signatures and symbols for
1126	the code the plan _decides_; do not spell out private helper internals — the

1128	designing interfaces".

1	# Discovery runtime design procedure (read for every plan; the `none` form is cheap)
2	
3	This reference holds the discovery procedure for the always-present `### Runtime design` subsection of `## Architecture Decisions`: the trigger surface, the full form, the `none — <reason>` form, the required pre-reads and the task shape. `discovery-instructions.md` step 5 names it at the gate site.
4	
5	## Runtime defaults
6	
7	Apply these to every full-form plan. A plan that departs from one names the departure and its reason on the `**Proportionality:**` line.
8	
9	- Durable work (anything that must survive the response, or a loop of paid or rate-limited calls) is queue-driven, not run in the request.
10	- A scheduler tick only enqueues one task per unit; it never runs the units itself.
11	- Every outbound call has an explicit timeout.
12	- Queue consumers are idempotent under redelivery, keyed on business identity rather than a per-attempt random value.
13	- All paid-call spend goes through one cap or ledger at a single choke point.
14	
15	The interactive budget behind "run in the request" is 10 s, never the platform's request timeout.
16	
17	## Step 5 sub-sections
18	
19	### Runtime design
20	
21	**Gate: the plan touches a runtime surface.** The trigger surface is the same as Instrumentation's: a plan that adds or changes a request handler, a background job or queue consumer, an outbound API call, a multi-stage pipeline, or a connection or worker pool. Decide the form from the plan's Task breakdown:
22	
23	- **Fires (full form):** "add a `POST /reports` endpoint that calls the model API five times"; "refresh every saved report nightly"; "call the billing API when an order completes".
24	- **Does NOT fire (`none` form):** docs-only, copy-only, style-only, test-only, dependency-bump and behaviour-preserving refactor plans; a UI-only change with no new request or job.
25	
26	The subsection is always present. A missing heading is ambiguous and a `none` is an explicit author affirmation, the same rule `## Instrumentation` uses.
27	
28	**Required pre-reads (full form only).**
29	
30	1. Read the skill at the path printed by `flow-module-status --skill-path flow-system-design`. A non-zero exit is a named skip, never a guessed path, and never a `bin/lib` import: discovery runs in the consumer worktree.
31	2. Read `--ref references/<platform>.md` for the repo's platform (`gcp`, `cloudflare` or `aws`), then every other reference whose "read when" line in the skill's Context list matches the change (data, workflows, rollout, caching, recovery, realtime, api). Each is a separate `flow-module-status --skill-path flow-system-design --ref <path>` call; a non-zero exit is a named skip.
32	3. Reuse the repo's existing primitives (queue, retry helper, spend ledger, idempotency table) before introducing new ones.
33	
34	**Full form.** Under `### Runtime design`, write:
35	
36	- A table `Operation | Est. p99 | Execution model | Timeout / deadline | Retries | Idempotency key | Cost bound`, one row per operation. An inline row may compress to `inline — <p99>, timeout <n>`. A cell that reuses a repo primitive names it in plain words (for example `existing spend ledger`), or `new`; the path goes on the touching task's `**Inputs:**` line, not in the table.
37	- A `**Platform:**` line: `gcp | cloudflare | aws | other`.
38	- A `**Proportionality:**` line naming what was deliberately left out (no queue for a 50 ms call; no sharding pre-launch).
39	- A `**Recovery:**` line whenever the Task breakdown adds or changes a table, migration or bucket: either the recovery path (backups or point-in-time recovery, object versioning, and how a restore is checked), or `none — <why the data is regenerable or already covered>`. Read `references/recovery.md` for the targets.
40	
41	**`none` form.** A single line `none — <reason>`, where the reason names why no runtime surface changes (for example `none — docs-only change` or `none — refactor-only, no behaviour change`). A bare `none` with no reason is a plan-lint miss, and so is a `none` whose tasks list runtime file paths without a refactor-only or no-behaviour-change reason, or a `none` while `## Instrumentation` is not `none`.
42	
43	**Task shape (full form only).** A task that adds a worker or queue consumer names its idempotency key and its timeout in its acceptance criterion. When a row reuses a primitive, the touching task lists that primitive's repo-relative path under `**Inputs:**` (a new one reads `new: <path>`). The task that creates a store with a non-`none` Recovery line sets up its backups, point-in-time recovery or versioning and a restore check. A task that creates or configures a queue sets the platform's must-set settings: SQS needs a visibility timeout above the consumer timeout and a dead-letter queue; Cloud Tasks needs a dispatch deadline and max attempts; Pub/Sub needs an ack deadline and a dead-letter topic; Cloudflare Queues needs a dead-letter queue. Prose in a reference is not enough, the setting must be in the task.
44	
45	**Forward pointer.** `flow-plan-lint` names a missing subsection, an empty body, a reason-less `none`, a table-less or Proportionality-less non-`none` body, a `none` on runtime file paths, a datastore change with no `**Recovery:**` line (or a recovery path with no backup or restore task), and a queue whose must-set settings are missing from the Task breakdown; it is advisory, so the miss is named in the plan summary at approval. `/flow-new-feature` Step 5 reads the subsection and, when it is not `none`, threads the skill's paths into the implementer's `skill_docs`.
46

1	# Discovery instrumentation procedure (read for every plan that touches a runtime surface)
2	
3	This reference holds the discovery procedure for the always-present `## Instrumentation` plan section: the trigger surface, the full form, the `none — <reason>` form, the required pre-reads, the task shape, and the omit-when-none PR-draft section. `discovery-instructions.md` step 5 names it at the gate site.
4	
5	## Step 5 sub-sections
6	
7	### Instrumentation
8	
9	**Gate: the plan touches a runtime surface.** The trigger surface is a plan that adds or changes a request handler, a background job or queue consumer, an outbound API call, a multi-stage pipeline, or a connection or worker pool. Decide the form from the plan's Task breakdown:
10	
11	- **Fires (full form):** "add a `POST /shares` endpoint"; "add a nightly export job"; "call the billing API when an order completes"; "split the import into fetch, parse and write stages".
12	- **Does NOT fire (`none` form):** docs-only, copy-only, style-only, test-only, dependency-bump and behaviour-preserving refactor plans; a UI-only change with no new request or job.
13	
14	The section is always present. A missing heading is ambiguous and a `none` is an explicit author affirmation, the same rule the PR description already uses.
15	
16	**Required pre-reads (full form only).**
17	
18	1. Read the repo's committed `.flow/metrics.md` as REQUIRED context when it exists. Reuse its `## Namespace`, its `## Attributes`, its `## error.type values`, its `## Helper` path, its `## Dashboards` and its existing `## SLOs`; never redefine them.
19	2. Read the metrics skill at the path printed by `flow-module-status --skill-path flow-metrics` (and `--ref references/conventions.md` for the naming and cardinality rules). A non-zero exit is a named skip, never a guessed path, and never a `bin/lib` import: discovery runs in the consumer worktree.
20	
21	**Full form.** Under `## Instrumentation`, write:
22	
23	- A `**Contract:**` line naming `.flow/metrics.md` `create` or `extend`.
24	- `### Metrics` — a table `Metric | Instrument | Unit | Attributes (closed values) | Emitted at`, one row per metric; the Instrument column may name a Gauge or UpDownCounter, and a metric the platform already emits has `Emitted at: platform-native (<source>)`. Follow with one line per operation: `Estimated series: <n> per operation` (the product of attribute-value counts, multiplied by (boundary count + 3) for a histogram: one bucket per boundary, `+Inf`, and `_sum`/`_count`; a gauge or up-down counter is the product of attribute-value counts, with no bucket multiplier; all counts are per reporting instance, so state when a justification is fleet-wide; the formula is in the skill's `references/conventions.md`).
25	- An `**Attributes:**` line: `reuses registered`, or the new keys with their closed values, which become `.flow/metrics.md` `## Attributes` rows.
26	- `### Error types` — the new `error.type` values with their meaning, or `reuses existing`.
27	- `### Dashboard panels` — the panels this change adds to `.flow/metrics.md` `## Dashboard panels`, each naming the dashboard it lands on.
28	- `### Alerts` — the saturation threshold rows this change adds to `.flow/metrics.md` `## Alerts`, or `burn-rate tiers only`.
29	- `### SLO` — `rolls into <SLO name>`, or a new journey SLO with its SLI and target. A new SLO is only for a new user journey.
30	- An `**As-code:**` line naming the dashboard or alert file paths the change updates, or `spec-only — <why>`.
31	
32	Default to the skill's shape: one duration histogram per operation split by `operation.outcome` (plus the keys the conventions instruments table allows for it) plus a failures counter split by `error.type`, a per-stage histogram for multi-stage operations, outbound-call histograms per dependency, and saturation signals for queue consumers and pools (backlog and oldest-message age, in-flight count, pool usage), platform-native first. Do not plan a hand-written edge metric where auto-instrumentation already emits it.
33	
34	**`none` form.** A single line `none — <reason>`, where the reason names why no trigger surface changes (for example `none — docs-only change` or `none — refactor-only, no behaviour change`). A bare `none` with no reason is a plan-lint miss, and so is a `none` whose tasks list runtime file paths (a route, server, worker, job, queue or cron file) without a refactor-only or no-behaviour-change reason.
35	
36	**Task shape (full form only).** At least one task's `**Files:**` includes the repo-local metrics helper (or its creation) and `.flow/metrics.md`. Its description names the planned metrics and `error.type` values so the edit-set intent carries them to the implementer, and its acceptance criterion asserts emission (an emission test against the helper's in-memory recorder) for the metrics the application emits; a platform-native metric needs no emission test.
37	
38	**PR draft section.** In `.flow-tmp/pr-description-draft.md`, add an omit-when-none `## Instrumentation` section between `## Key decisions` and `## Deviations from plan`: the metrics, panels and alert/SLO spec distilled from the plan section. It links the dashboard URL from `.flow/metrics.md` `## Dashboards` and names the panels the change adds, or says `spec-only` when no URL exists yet; never a per-panel URL, which most backends do not have. With `backend: none yet`, only the PR that creates `.flow/metrics.md` carries the full note that graphs need a backend choice; later PRs carry one line saying these metrics are recorded but won't show on any graph until a metrics backend is chosen (status in `.flow/metrics.md` `## Backend`). Omit the heading entirely when the plan section is `none`.
39	
40	**Forward pointer.** `/flow-new-feature` Step 5 reads the plan's `## Instrumentation` and, when it is not `none`, threads the metrics skill's paths into the implementer's `skill_docs`. `flow-plan-lint` names a missing section, a reason-less `none`, a table-less non-`none` section, a non-`none` section with no `**Attributes:**` line, and a `none` on runtime file paths; it is advisory, so the miss is named in the plan summary at approval.
41
